result.topic_en: Opening page of Euler's essay on fluid friction, noting that water flowing through pipes loses motion, more so in longer and narrower pipes, so fountains never reach the height predicted by theory, and arguing that theory is not refuted but must account for neglected circumstances.
result.transcription:
338 (o)
TENTAMEN
THEORIAE
DE
FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM.
Auctore
L. EVLERO.
1.
Experientia luculenter teſtatur, aquam, dum per canales promouetur, non exiguam pati motus ſui diminutionem, eamque eo magis eſſe notabilem, quo longiores fuerint, ſimulque arctiores, iſtiusmodi canales. Atque haec motus diminutio inprimis in fontibus ſalientibus deprehenditur, ad quos aqua per tubos, ſeu canales, deriuatur; cum enim, per Theoriam motus fluidorum, aqua fere ad eandem altitudinem aſſurgere deberet, ex qua lapſu ad orificium fontis deſcenderat, tamen teſte experientia hanc altitudinem nunquam attingit, ſed eo magis ab ea deficere ſolet, quo longiorem viam in tubis abſoluerit, et quo arctiores fuerint iſti tubi.
2. Quanquam ob hanc cauſam Theoria plerisque practicis non parum ſuſpecta videri ſolet, tamen cum ea principiis mechanicae certiſſimis ſit innixa, eius veritas ob hunc diſſenſum minime debilitatur, ſed potius cauſam iſtius aberrationis in eiusmodi circumſtantiis quaeri oportet, quae in Theoria non fuerint debito modo
con-

items.quote: Experientia luculenter teſtatur, aquam, dum per canales promouetur, non exiguam pati motus ſui diminutionem, eamque eo magis eſſe notabilem, quo longiores fuerint, ſimulque arctiores, iſtiusmodi canales.
items.english: Experience clearly shows that water, while driven through channels, suffers no small diminution of its motion, and that this is the more notable the longer and at the same time narrower such channels are.

items.quote:
ſed potius cauſam iſtius aberrationis in eiusmodi circumſtantiis quaeri oportet, quae in Theoria non fuerint debito modo
con-
items.english: but rather the cause of this deviation must be sought in those circumstances which have not been duly con[sidered] in the theory.
